provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The original rule has four parts. Isolated single foreground cells are erased to background. Each multi-cell glyph keeps its cells and is recoloured by the symmetry of its cropped bounding-box mask: up-down mirror gives 1, left-right mirror gives 3, and diagonal-only symmetry (square box, main or anti-diagonal) gives 6.

The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates:
- It takes the background as the most common colour.
- It finds 4-connected same-colour non-background components.
- It erases single-cell components.
- It tests each remaining crop for visible UD, LR and diagonal symmetry.

The factory sets the output colours from the D4 element. Reversing rows keeps both UD and LR symmetry, and only swaps main-diagonal with anti-diagonal symmetry. A quarter turn swaps UD with LR. So for an odd number of clockwise turns (d4%4 in {1,3}), visible UD shapes get palette[3] and visible LR shapes get palette[1]. Otherwise visible UD gets palette[1] and visible LR gets palette[3]. Diagonal-only shapes always get palette[6]. The background is inferred from pixels, so it is never mapped through the palette.

The constructor guarantees several things this relies on:
- Glyph boxes are separated by background and noise is 8-isolated, so 4- and 8-connectivity give the same components.
- The background stays the strict majority colour.
- No generated glyph is both UD and LR, so the classes never conflict.
- Every glyph crop is at least 3x3, so single cells are exactly the noise.
draft_notes.limitations: Glyphs that are both UD- and LR-symmetric, or have no symmetry, are left unchanged. The constructor never generates them, and its explicit-scene checker rejects them. The archived solver's 'UD checked first' precedence is not carried over as a visible rule, because it is not orientation-invariant and never arises in the domain. Two-cell objects are also outside the domain; they would be classified as UD/LR glyphs, not erased. The approved fixtures agree with the uniform rule; no contradictions or constructor defects were found. This code has not been run.
